text: Given a valid sla_id that exists in the tenant, When halopsa_sla_get is called with it, Then the result has id, name, and a priorities array where each item has id, name, responsetime, fixtime, colour

Given an SLA whose priority rows omit some of responsetime/fixtime/colour, or whose priorities list is empty, When halopsa_sla_get is called, Then the missing fields are omitted per row and an empty priorities list does not fail the call
Given an sla_id that does not exist in the tenant, When halopsa_sla_get is called, Then the result is a structured not_found error, not a raw exception or a disguised empty success
Given a missing or non-numeric sla_id, When halopsa_sla_get is called, Then the result is invalid_argument and no HTTP request is made to HaloPSA

Given credential headers for two different tenants, When halopsa_sla_get is called once per tenant with that tenant's own sla_id, Then each call returns only that tenant's SLA data and nothing is cached or shared across the two calls
steps: Send tools/call halopsa_sla_get with tenant A's X-Halo-* headers and an SLA id known to exist in tenant A
Send tools/call halopsa_sla_get with tenant B's X-Halo-* headers and an SLA id known to exist in tenant B
Compare both responses against each tenant's own HaloPSA instance
expect: Tenant A's response matches only tenant A's SLA (id/name/priorities); tenant B's response matches only tenant B's SLA; neither response leaks the other tenant's data
evidence: needs a real vendor account with at least two HaloPSA tenants/instances; none available in this environment (does not block the design or dev exit per references/mcp-track.md: a missing vendor test account is not a blocker)

text: Given halopsa_sla_get is registered, When tools/list is read, Then it appears with readOnlyHint=true and destructiveHint=false, and every pre-existing tool's name, required parameters and parameter types are unchanged
